name: UniversityFlow

tables.definition: Basic student information and current registration eligibility

columns.name: date_of_birth
columns.definition: Birth date; not an academic event

columns.name: registration_eligibility
columns.definition: Current eligibility: ELIGIBLE or INELIGIBLE; does not store when eligibility changed

columns.name: course_id
columns.definition: Course identifier; one course offering in this dataset

columns.name: instructor
columns.definition: Instructor name; the original schema has no separate instructor table

columns.name: class_time
columns.definition: Scheduled teaching time; not proof that a class took place

tables.definition: Successful student-course registrations; one row per student and course

columns.name: course_id
columns.definition: Course identifier; one course offering in this dataset

columns.name: registration_time
columns.definition: Actual successful course-registration time in UTC

columns.name: status
columns.definition: Current registration status; REGISTERED in this dataset; no status-change history is stored

tables.definition: Degree examination results; repeated examinations use separate result IDs

columns.name: grade
columns.definition: Examination score from 0 to 100; 60 is the synthetic eligibility threshold

columns.name: examination_date
columns.definition: Actual examination time in UTC; not the time its result was published

value_domain.ELIGIBLE: Student may register after passing the simulated examination
value_domain.INELIGIBLE: Student has no passing examination in the simulated history

business_rules: Use each student as a case (one timeline).
An examination-result row records one Degree Examination Taken event at examination_date. The timestamp does not establish when the result was published.
A registration row records one Course Registered event at registration_time.
The default student timeline contains recorded examination events and successful registrations.
Students may retake the examination. In this simulation a score of at least 60 permits subsequent registration. The source does not specify this threshold.
The student-course composite key allows only one retained registration per pair. Repeated registrations and withdrawals are not added.
Eligibility and status are current values. Their transitions cannot be reconstructed.
Birth dates and scheduled class times are not academic process events.
The requirement mentions notification and information checks, but their execution times are not stored.
Students with no selected events remain in the separately declared case population.
